title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: how many accounts one customer may hold
content:
## Policy clause

A customer may hold several Savings & Money Market Accounts. Before a new account is opened, two caps are tested against the bank's account records for that customer:

1. **Portfolio cap.** The number of the customer's savings accounts whose status is not closed must be below 6.
2. **Tier cap.** The number of the customer's savings accounts of the requested tier whose status is not closed must be below that tier's per-customer account limit.

Accounts in applied, active and dormant status count toward both caps; closed accounts never count. When either cap has been reached, the opening is declined and nothing is recorded.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** Both counts come from the system record of the customer's savings accounts and their current statuses, taken before the opening is recorded. What the customer says about the accounts they hold does not replace the record.
- **Object correlation.** The portfolio cap counts every savings account of the same customer. The tier cap counts only that customer's accounts whose tier is the tier requested for the new account.
- **Tier values.** The portfolio cap of 6 is one figure for the whole product. The tier cap is the per-customer account limit of the requested tier; each of the six tiers has its own limit.

## Condition table

| Portfolio count (not closed) | Tier count (not closed) versus the requested tier's limit | Outcome under this policy |
|---|---|---|
| below 6 | below the limit | the caps do not stand in the way of the opening |
| below 6 | not below the limit | opening declined, nothing recorded |
| not below 6 | below the limit | opening declined, nothing recorded |
| not below 6 | not below the limit | opening declined, nothing recorded |

## Worked cases (hypothetical customers)

- **Case A.** A customer holds five savings accounts: two active, one dormant, one applied and one closed. The not-closed count is four, which is below 6, so the portfolio cap does not block a new account; the tier cap is then tested for the requested tier.
- **Case B.** A customer holds six accounts, all active or dormant, and closed a seventh last year. The not-closed count is 6, which is not below 6, so any new opening is declined whatever tier is requested.
- **Case C.** A customer's accounts of the requested tier that are not closed already number as many as that tier's limit, one of them still in applied status awaiting its first deposit. The applied account counts, so the tier cap is reached and the opening is declined.

## Points of judgement

**Does an account that was never funded and has since been closed as unfunded still count?** No; it is closed, and closed accounts never count.

**Does a dormant account count?** Yes; dormant accounts count toward both caps.
